# Porting an xscreensaver hack

The rules live in `AGENTS.md` ("Rules", "Gotchas") and the path-scoped notes in
`.claude/rules/`. This skill sets the order of work and the points to stop. The
numbered steps are in `adding-a-hack.md` and the recipes it names are in
`techniques.md`, both next to this file. For several hacks in one go, read
`batches.md` too.

## 1. Pick, then read the source

Take S-rated rows from `docs/porting-assessment.md` first, and prefer a low
**Speed** band: the table runs each unported S hack on the host. The effort
rating counts missing shim calls, not memory, speed or stack (Braid was S, and
would have shown as high). A high band is a hack that will probably run slowly
on the board; a low band is not a guarantee, because a hack still doing
software `double` maths runs far slower on the device than on the host. Read
the hack's source before copying it, and look for:

| The source has | Technique (seen in) |
| --- | --- |
| Arrays or a state over a few MB | Build-time patch (Maze) |
| `sin`, `cos`, `sqrt`, `pow`, `double` in a hot loop | Single precision (Galaxy, Substrate) |
| Locals over a few KB | Stack check (Rorschach) |
| An allocation of 100 KB or more, or `exit()` on failure | Large allocations (Substrate) |
| Pixmaps, clip masks, a logo image | Images (Maze) |
| A hack that restarts itself | Restart leak test (Maze, Substrate) |
| A `free` that relies on state `draw` sets up (a lazy `initted`) | Stopping before the first draw (Blaster) |
| Hairlines, fades or `glPolygonOffset` in a GL hack | Thin lines in a GL hack |
| Xft text (`XftDrawStringUtf8`) | Xft text (XJack) |
| Threads, shared memory | Skipping a hack |
| A licence header | Read it; add a notices section only if it differs from jwz's |

## 2. Set up

Work in a worktree off `origin/main`. Its setup and the commands it refuses are
in "Worktree setup".

## 3. Red, copy, green

Follow `adding-a-hack.md`. Show the registry test failing before
copying. Fill each shim gap test-first, then break the code on purpose and
watch the test fail ("Tests that cannot be fooled"). Filling a missing
function is a shim gap. Changing what every hack sees (the runner, a default, a
shared helper) is not: stop and ask Rod first. A speed-up in the shared GL
layer counts too, even when every pinned frame hash still matches (HexTrail's
deferred depth clear): ask before writing it, and name it in the PR body.

## 4. Verify on the host

Run `pio test -e native`, `uv run --with pytest --with pillow pytest tools/tests`
and `uv run tools/check_notices.py`, and dump frames at several counts. Host
frames cannot show a byte swap, which happens in the push to the display: judge
colour on the device, on a colour you know the answer to.

## 5. Device

Flash only after Rod says so in this conversation; approval for one flash is
not approval for the next. See "Device capture". Report "compiles", "host tests
pass" and "runs on the device" separately; only Rod can say what the screen
shows. If it is slow, measure, change one thing, flash again and compare; if it
is still slow, say so and suggest dropping it. A hack that runs at a good rate
can still go: Rod dropped Boing (8.3 fps, "pretty boring on a small screen")
and asked for HexTrail to be tuned because it fell under 10 fps before the
rotation moved on. Judge a hack on a 466 px round screen, and by its worst
window as well as its mean. Record the numbers in
`tools/assessment_measured.md.in`, marking anything unmeasured as such.

## 6. Deliver

Commit named paths. Open the draft PR with `entire trail create` and put what
is unverified in its body. After a rebase, a push needs `--force-with-lease`:
ask Rod each time. Rod approves and merges; then delete the branch and
fast-forward `main`. New gotchas go in the matching `.claude/rules/` file (or
`AGENTS.md` if they apply everywhere) in the same PR, and deferred
ideas become issues.

## Red flags

| Thought | Reality |
| --- | --- |
| "It is rated S, so I need not read it" | Maze was rated L for Xlib gaps; the real blocker was a 20 MB `calloc`. |
| "It compiles, so it works" | Rorschach compiled and rebooted on its first frame. |
| "The colours look right" | Not from a host frame: every hack was byte swapped until Maze. |
| "My test passes, so it tests something" | A test through Pyro passed with the runner broken. Break the code on purpose. |
| "AGENTS.md says to fix shim gaps, so I can change the runner" | A new function is a gap. A change every hack sees needs Rod. |
| "Rod approved flashing earlier" | Ask again for each flash. |
| "Single precision is done, so the hack is as fast as it gets" | HexTrail gained 0.3 fps from it and 2.3 from a depth clear in the GL layer. Read what the shared code does each frame. |
| "The mean is above 10 fps" | HexTrail's mean was 15.3 and its worst window 10.8; its step grew all cycle. Read the lowest window. |

Deluxe: ideas for more than 11-13 fps
open
Deluxe runs at 10.4-12.8 fps on the board (step 44.6-62.6 ms, push 32.5 ms).
These are ideas to get more out of it, none tried yet. Numbers are from the
Deluxe section of `tools/assessment_measured.md`.

## Where the time goes

- On the device a frame is the step and the push one after the other:
  about 47 ms plus 32.5 ms is about 80 ms, which is the 12 fps we see.
- A host profile put 94% of the original frame in the wide circles, which
  `stroke_circle` fixed (2-5 fps became 13-15 fps, opaque).
- Translucency added 13 ms a step on the board, and the mask that stops
  overlaps blending twice added another 3-5 ms, though it costs nothing on the
  host. So the host cannot rank these ideas: split the device step with a
  temporary flag that returns early from each part before changing anything.

## Ideas, biggest first

1. **Overlap the push with the next step.** Draw into a second canvas while the
   first is pushed. The step would no longer wait for the push, so the frame
   would take the longer of the two (about 47 ms, 21 fps) instead of the sum.
   This is the same push-overlap item still open for the GL hacks, and it
   would help every hack whose step is more than a few milliseconds.
2. **Shrink the mask.** Each multi-piece shape does a 27 KB `calloc` and scans
   every row and word of the canvas. Track the rows and words a shape touched,
   scan and clear only those, or keep one buffer instead of allocating each
   time (a static buffer would need the leak tests to expect it).
3. **Blend faster.** `blend_box` swaps every pixel to blend and swaps it back.
   Blending two pixels per 32-bit word, or in the swapped domain, would cut
   the per-pixel work. Long runs go through one call per run.
4. **Draw a star as one polygon.** A star is ten segments plus ten joins
   today. Filling its outline once would mean far fewer fills and no mask.
5. **Single precision in `draw_star`.** It does ten `cos` and ten `sin` in
   software `double` per star per frame. Small beside the rest, but a
   single-precision wrapper is cheap (`techniques.md`).
6. **Cheaper erase.** The hack fills the whole canvas black each frame and the
   push sends all 466 rows. Little to gain while shapes cover most of the
   screen, but worth a check on the frames where they do not.

## Not measured yet

- PSRAM against an idle build, a lap soak with the rotation on, and a long run.
  PSRAM was flat at 7,327,227 in every capture and heap held at 322,648-323,056
  bytes over 45 seconds.

content.text:
I've done the first, read-only pass. I built for the device without flashing and attributed every software-`double` call to its function. Nothing is changed or committed, and nothing is measured on the board yet. #54 fits only partly: its idea 5 is soft-double, but the rest of it isn't.

**What the objects show**

| Issue | Where the soft-double is | Whose code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #57 Halftone | `canvas_fill_ellipse` (`core/canvas.c`) has a `sqrt`, `ceil`, `floor` and a `__divdf3` per row. Halftone's own `halftone_init` has some, but only at init. | Shared |
| #74 | `canvas_fill_polygon` has a `__divdf3`, two `ceil`s and `__fixdfdi` conversions. | Shared |
| #98 Lisa and wide lines | `stroke.c` is soft-double throughout. `disc` has 8 `__muldf3`, 2 `sqrt` and 2 `__divdf3`, and `stroke_segment_ends` has 8 `__adddf3`. `canvas_line` is also soft-double. | Shared |
| #59 Anemone | `anemone_direct` has only one `__divdf3` and one truncation, both in init. The hack itself is clean, so the cost is almost certainly the stroker's width-6 caps (`disc`). That also ties it to #98. | Shared |
| #59 Interaggregate | `build_field` still has 16 `__divdf3`, 16 `__muldf3` and 23 float-to-double widenings. It is a wrapper, so I can fix it without touching shared code. | Ours |
| #75 `frand` | `single_frand.h` already exists. Fireworkx's only leftover is two widenings in `fs_roll_rgb`. This looks mostly done, and I'd check which wrappers don't include it yet. | Ours |
| #54 Deluxe | Only idea 5 (`draw_star` doing `cos` and `sin` in `double`) is soft-double. Push overlap, mask size and blend speed are different problems. | Mixed |

So #57, #74 and #98 are really one change: a float or integer rewrite of the ellipse, polygon and stroker code in the shared canvas. Anemone and Deluxe would probably gain from it too. Interaggregate, #75 and #54's idea 5 can be done in wrappers.

**Limits of this pass**
- This is static attribution. It shows a function contains software `double` maths, not that the function is hot. I haven't checked how often `build_field` runs, for example.
- The #57 estimate (about 12 fps rather than 15) is the agent's guess from the issue. I haven't verified it.

**Proposed order**
1. **Wrapper-only fixes first, with no shared-code risk:** Interaggregate's `build_field`, any wrapper missing `single_frand.h`, and Deluxe's `draw_star`. I'd measure each on the host and then ask you before any flash.
2. **Measure Lisa at each width 1–8 on the host,** as #98 asks, to find where the stroker spends its time. Do the same for Anemone's segment count.
3. **Prototype a float or integer `canvas_fill_ellipse` and `canvas_fill_polygon`** behind host tests. Compare pinned frame hashes and tell you which hacks move. I'd write nothing into shared code until you approve.

I'd leave #54's push overlap out. It's an architectural change that also covers the GL hacks, so it's a separate decision.

Do you want me to start on step 1 and 2 now? And are you happy for me to prototype step 3 on a branch, with the shared-code change only landing if you approve it?
Great.  Yeah, start working on this.  I'm off out for the day so I'll catch up with you later. See how much progress you can make without access to the device.

# Working in a git worktree

Moved verbatim from AGENTS.md.

- In a git worktree the ignored `vendor/`, `.venv/` and `.platformio/` are
  missing. Symlink them from the main checkout. `.gitignore`'s trailing slashes
  don't match symlinks, so they would show as untracked, but the shared
  `.git/info/exclude` already lists the three names. That file is shared by
  every worktree: ask Rod before adding to it.
  The harness refuses `source tools/env.sh` and a computed `PATH` there: run
  `PLATFORMIO_CORE_DIR=<worktree>/.platformio ../.venv/bin/pio ...` instead,
  and keep commands plain (no scripts, loops, `$VAR` in a command or `&&`
  chains with a computed path). A worktree an agent works in (`isolation:
  "worktree"`) starts from `origin/main`, not from your branch, and has no
  vendor or toolchain until you link them.
  It also refuses heredocs, `git -C` and `cd` into another worktree: use the
  Edit and Write tools. It refuses `git ... | tar` and `cd <dir> && git ...`
  too: use `git archive -o f.tar <sha>` then `tar -x -f f.tar -C <dir>`, and run
  git from the worktree root. A background shell starts there as well, so use
  `pio test -d <abs>/firmware` with absolute paths. Parallel calls can race
  (a `uv run` in the root disturbed `.venv` while `pio` ran:
  "../.venv/bin/pio: no such file"), so run
  `uv` and `pio` one at a time. To fast-forward `main` or remove the worktree,
  leave it first with `ExitWorktree keep`. If no checkout has `main` out,
  `git fetch origin main:main` fast-forwards it from anywhere.
  Before `ExitWorktree remove` on a merged branch, check
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor <tip> origin/main`; the tool's "discarded N
  commits" count ignores merges. `.platformio`, `.venv` and `vendor` there are
  symlinks, so removal leaves the real ones alone. After a merge,
  `ExitWorktree keep` names a branch (`worktree-<name>`) that may not exist:
  remove the worktree with `git worktree remove --force <path>` and delete the
  real branch, as separate commands, because a failed `&&` link skips the rest
  silently. Check `git worktree list` afterwards. In a session resumed from a
  summary, `ExitWorktree` is a no-op ("no active EnterWorktree session"):
  remove the worktree with `git worktree remove --force <path>` from the main
  checkout instead. To delete the merged branch
  you are standing on, `git switch --detach origin/main` in the worktree first.
  The shell's directory resets after each command and after `ExitWorktree`, so
  use absolute paths (`../.venv/bin/pio` failed from the wrong place and the run
  looked like a test failure). A loop over several mutations is refused as a
  command: write it as a script in the scratchpad that edits the file, runs
  `pio test` through `subprocess` and restores the file in `finally`, then run
  it with `python3 -I`.
  Stopping such a script (TaskStop) kills it before `finally` runs: check
  `git diff` afterwards and restore the file by hand.
  Also refused: a heredoc (use the Write tool for a scratchpad script), `$(...)`
  inside a git command, and the quoted `PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS` above combined
  with a redirect or `NO_COLOR=1`. Flashing worked as
  `PLATFORMIO_CORE_DIR=<wt>/.platformio PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS="..."
  .venv/bin/pio run -d firmware -e stopwatch -t upload` with no redirect: the
  540 KB of output lands in a tool-results file, so grep that for "Hash of data
  verified". Edit and Write refuse the main checkout's path while you are in a
  worktree. `pio test -f test_x` runs the whole suite (`test_hacks` takes 3
  minutes, the full native run 7), and a failing summary reads "2 failed, 101
  succeeded": match `[FAILED]` or the return code, not "succeeded".

/* Builds the unmodified interaggregate.c in single precision (the ESP32-S3's FPU is
 * single-precision only, so `double` maths runs in software) and
 * with its decimal literals made floats at build time
 * (tools/float_literals.py), or `0.5 * x` would stay software double, with HAVE_JWXYZ
 * defined after the framework headers. Upstream defines it where the window
 * system double-buffers for the hack, and the hack then draws straight on the
 * window. The shim can draw into pixmaps, but a back buffer would cost 434 KB
 * and a full-frame copy each frame, and would dirty every row. */
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "screenhack.h"

#include "core/canvas.h"
#include "hacks/single_precision.h"

/* Interaggregate's alpha blend takes the red, green and blue bits out of
 * pixel values itself (point2rgb), assuming ordinary RGB565. The canvas holds
 * the bytes swapped, so swap where a colour comes back from XAllocColor and
 * where it goes into XSetForeground, which leaves the hack working in ordinary
 * RGB565. Its own foreground and background are black and white, which are the
 * same in either order, so get_pixel_resource needs no wrapper unless those
 * defaults change. */
static Status interaggregate_alloc_color(Display *dpy, Colormap cmap, XColor *c) {
  Status ok = XAllocColor(dpy, cmap, c);
  c->pixel = px_swap((uint16_t)c->pixel);
  return ok;
}
#define XAllocColor interaggregate_alloc_color
#define XSetForeground(dpy, gc, pixel) \
  XSetForeground(dpy, gc, px_swap((uint16_t)(pixel)))

#undef XSCREENSAVER_MODULE
#define XSCREENSAVER_MODULE(CLASS, PREFIX)
#define HAVE_JWXYZ
#undef M_PI
#define M_PI 3.14159265358979323846f

#include "interaggregate_floatlit.c"

"""Make every decimal literal in a C file a float, for single-precision builds.

`hacks/single_precision.h` turns the keyword `double` into `float`, but a
literal such as `0.5` is still a double, so `0.5 * x` with a float `x` is done
in double precision, which the ESP32-S3 does in software (Braid's draw loop
called `__muldf3` and `__adddf3` for every coordinate). Giving each literal an
`f` suffix keeps the arithmetic in single precision.

GCC's `-fsingle-precision-constant` does the same, but Apple clang ignores it,
so host tests would run different arithmetic from the board. A source rewrite
gives both the same text.

The copied hack stays byte-identical to upstream. The firmware build writes a
rewritten copy with `firmware/patch_float_literals.py` and compiles that.
"""

import re

_TOKEN = re.compile(
    r"""
      (?P<skip>
          /\*.*?\*/
        | //[^\n]*
        | "(?:\\.|[^"\\\n])*"
        | '(?:\\.|[^'\\\n])*'
      )
    | (?P<literal>
          (?:\d+\.\d+|\.\d+|\d+\.(?![\w.]))(?![\w.])
      )
    """,
    re.VERBOSE | re.DOTALL,
)


def float_literals(source: str) -> str:
    """Appends `f` to each decimal literal outside strings, characters and
    comments. A literal with a suffix or an exponent is left as it is."""
    count = 0

    def replace(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
        nonlocal count
        if match.group("skip") is not None:
            return match.group(0)
        count += 1
        return match.group(0) + "f"

    out = _TOKEN.sub(replace, source)
    if count == 0:
        raise ValueError("no floating-point literals found; is this the right file?")
    return out

"""Lists the software-double calls in the device build's objects, by function.

The ESP32-S3's FPU is single-precision only, so `double` arithmetic and libm
calls become library calls (`__muldf3`, `sqrt`, ...) that cost tens to hundreds
of cycles. A wrapper that still shows them in a per-frame function has a
literal or a macro the single-precision header could not reach (`frand`,
`MAXRAND`, `M_PI`). This reads what the compiler produced, so it needs a device
build: `pio run -e stopwatch` from `firmware/`.

    uv run tools/softdouble_report.py              # every hack object
    uv run tools/softdouble_report.py galaxy_single x11shim/stroke
"""

import re
import subprocess
import sys
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OBJDUMP = next(
    (ROOT / ".platformio/packages/toolchain-xtensa-esp32s3/bin").glob(
        "xtensa-esp32s3-elf-objdump"
    ),
    None,
)
BUILD = ROOT / "firmware/.pio/build/stopwatch/src"

SOFT = re.compile(
    r"R_XTENSA_\w+\s+(__\w*df\w*|sqrt|floor|ceil|sin|cos|pow|atan2?|log|exp)\s*$"
)
FUNCTION = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]+ <(.+)>:")


def soft_calls(obj: Path) -> dict[str, Counter]:
    """Soft-double references per function in one object file."""
    assert OBJDUMP is not None, "toolchain not found: link .platformio into the repo"
    listing = subprocess.run(
        [str(OBJDUMP), "-dr", "--no-show-raw-insn", str(obj)],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    ).stdout
    found: dict[str, Counter] = defaultdict(Counter)
    function = None
    for line in listing.splitlines():
        if m := FUNCTION.match(line):
            function = m.group(1)
        elif function and not function.startswith(".literal"):
            if m := SOFT.search(line):
                found[function][m.group(1)] += 1
    return found


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    if not BUILD.is_dir():
        raise SystemExit(f"no device build at {BUILD}: run pio run -e stopwatch")
    wanted = argv or [""]
    objects = sorted(
        p
        for p in BUILD.rglob("*.o")
        if any(w in str(p.relative_to(BUILD)) for w in wanted)
        and (argv or "hacks/" in str(p))
    )
    for obj in objects:
        found = soft_calls(obj)
        total = sum(sum(c.values()) for c in found.values())
        print(f"{obj.relative_to(BUILD)}: {total}")
        for function, calls in sorted(found.items(), key=lambda kv: -sum(kv[1].values())):
            print(f"    {function}: {dict(calls)}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

import float_literals as fl

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
BRAID_C = ROOT / "firmware" / "src" / "hacks" / "braid" / "braid.c"


def test_decimal_literals_become_float():
    assert fl.float_literals("x = 0.5 * (1.0 + y) / 12.0;") == (
        "x = 0.5f * (1.0f + y) / 12.0f;"
    )


def test_leading_and_trailing_point_forms():
    assert fl.float_literals("a = .5 + 5.;") == "a = .5f + 5.f;"


def test_literals_that_already_have_a_suffix_are_left_alone():
    assert fl.float_literals("a = 2.0f + 3.0L + 4.0;") == "a = 2.0f + 3.0L + 4.0f;"


def test_integers_member_access_and_identifiers_are_left_alone():
    source = "n = 15 + v.x + arr[1].y + p->a1.b + x2.c;"
    assert fl.float_literals(source + " k = 1.5;") == source + " k = 1.5f;"


def test_strings_comments_and_chars_are_left_alone():
    source = '"*delay: 1.0 \\n" /* 2.0 */ // 3.0\nc = \'.\'; s = "a\\"4.0"; z = 6.0;'
    out = fl.float_literals(source)
    assert '"*delay: 1.0 \\n"' in out
    assert "/* 2.0 */" in out
    assert "// 3.0\n" in out
    assert "'.'" in out
    assert '"a\\"4.0"' in out

"""compare.py old_program new_program out_prefix name:index:frames[,frames] ..."""
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image

old, new, prefix = sys.argv[1:4]


def load(p):
    data = Path(p).read_bytes()
    im = Image.new("RGB", (466, 466))
    px = im.load()
    for i in range(466 * 466):
        v = data[2 * i] | (data[2 * i + 1] << 8)
        r, g, b = (v >> 11) & 31, (v >> 5) & 63, v & 31
        px[i % 466, i // 466] = (r << 3 | r >> 2, g << 2 | g >> 4, b << 3 | b >> 2)
    return im


for spec in sys.argv[4:]:
    name, idx, frames = spec.split(":")
    for n in frames.split(","):
        outs = []
        for tag, prog in (("old", old), ("new", new)):
            raw = f"{prefix}_{name}_{n}_{tag}.raw"
            subprocess.run([prog, idx, n, raw], check=True, capture_output=True)
            outs.append(load(raw))
        sbs = Image.new("RGB", (942, 466), (60, 60, 60))
        sbs.paste(outs[0], (0, 0))
        sbs.paste(outs[1], (476, 0))
        sbs.save(f"{prefix}_{name}_{n}.png")

43	  reopen it in a loop. Opening the port resets the board
44	  (`rst:0x15 USB_UART_CHIP_RESET`, even with DTR/RTS held low): the overlay
45	  returns to nothing and a random hack starts. To measure one hack, flash a
46	  pinned build (`START_HACK` plus `ROTATE_SECONDS=0`), start the capture, then
47	  tap during it: the early windows are the baseline, the later ones have the
48	  overlay.
49	  Set `dtr` and `rts` to False on an unopened `serial.Serial()` before
50	  `open()`: a reopen loop without that once parked the chip in its bootloader
51	  (`boot:0x3 ... waiting for download`, screen frozen). Recover, or reset just
52	  before a capture to log from boot (a hack's `fprintf(stderr)` reaches the
53	  log), with `.venv/bin/python .platformio/packages/tool-esptoolpy/esptool.py
54	  --chip esp32s3 --port /dev/cu.usbmodem112401 --after hard_reset read_mac`.
55	- Flash with `pio run -e stopwatch -t upload > file 2>&1`, never piped through
56	  `head`, and check for "Hash of data verified". The button steps backwards
57	  (Pyro, then Lightning, then Drift...). Work out how long a restart takes
58	  from the hack's cycle count times its frame time (Substrate: 10,000 cycles
59	  at about 160 ms is 27 minutes) and capture that long, with rotation off.
60	- `ad-flyingtoasters` force flags (add to `PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS`):
61	  `-DAD_TOASTERS_ART=0|1` (0 is 1-bit, 1 is colour) and
62	  `-DAD_TOASTERS_DONENESS=0|1|2` (light, medium, dark) and
63	  `-DAD_TOASTERS_SCALE=1|2` (2 is the default, with 6 flyers; 1 is the
64	  original size, with 10); a number outside those is an `#error`. It logs
65	  `ad-flyingtoasters: <art>, doneness=<level>` to stderr at start.
66	- To see where a GL hack's frame goes, add `-DGL_PROFILE`: a `glprof` line
67	  follows each `run` line with time per stage (clear, list, vertex, shade,
68	  tri, fill, point, line; nested, so vertex includes tri and fill). Time left
69	  over is the hack's own code. To compare builds, `.venv/bin/python -I
70	  tools/ab_flash.py --hack Gears --seconds 60 --rounds 2 --out <dir>
71	  "a=-DGL_PROFILE" "b=-DGL_PROFILE -DFOO"` builds each variant pinned, flashes
72	  them in turn and tabulates the windows. It flashes: run it only with Rod's
73	  go-ahead. It builds each hack's variants from the working tree when that
74	  hack's turn starts, so leave `src/` and `tools/tinygl_patch.py` alone until
75	  the last hack has built. It compares flag variants of one tree: to A/B a
76	  change, put it behind a temporary `-D` switch (as `-DPUSH_NO_DISC` does).
77	  It takes one `--hack` per run: loop several from a scratchpad script run
78	  with `run_in_background`, and `touch` a done file at the end.
79	- `esptool` reads of the 16 MB flash need `--baud 921600` (about 3.5 minutes)
80	  and show no progress when piped.
81	- Another session may be using the board. Before flashing, run `lsof
82	  /dev/cu.usbmodem112401`: a "multiple access on port" upload error was
83	  another session's serial capture, and esptool's connect resets the board
84	  under it. Ask Rod before flashing over someone else's run.
85	- PlatformIO cleans the build directory, image and all, when

HexTrail: give the hack a float XYZ, so vertex maths is not software double

Each hexagon's pos and every corner are XYZ, which normals.h declares with
double fields before single_precision.h can rename them. Every vertex
(h->pos.x + corners[j].x * size1) therefore promoted to double: draw_hextrail
had 94 soft-double calls in its object. The hack only stores XYZ (it never
calls calc_normal), so normals.h now sees its own name for the double struct
and the hack gets a float one in this translation unit.

draw_hextrail goes from 94 soft-double calls to 4. Frames are byte-identical
at 200 and 1500 frames (the pinned hash did not move), so this is free of
visual risk. Found with -Wdouble-promotion on the device compile command.

"""Find (w, h, dy2) where the float estimate of the ellipse half-span is wrong."""
import math

import numpy as np

f32 = np.float32
found_down, found_up = [], []
for h in range(1, 400):
    for w in range(1, 400):
        for dy2 in range(-(h - 1), h, 2 if (h - 1) % 2 == 0 else 2):
            pass
        # dy2 has the parity of (h - 1): dy2 = 2*row - h + 1
        for row in range(h):
            dy2 = 2 * row - h + 1
            q = h * h - dy2 * dy2
            limit = w * w * q
            est = int(f32(f32(math.sqrt(0) + 0) if False else np.sqrt(f32(q))) * f32(w) / f32(h))
            # exact: largest s with s*s*h*h <= limit
            s = math.isqrt(limit // (h * h))
            while (s + 1) * (s + 1) * h * h <= limit:
                s += 1
            while s * s * h * h > limit:
                s -= 1
            if est > s:
                found_down.append((w, h, row, est, s))
            elif est < s:
                found_up.append((w, h, row, est, s))
    if len(found_down) > 5 and len(found_up) > 5:
        break
print("estimate too big (needs the down loop):", found_down[:6])
print("estimate too small (needs the up loop):", found_up[:6])
print(len(found_down), len(found_up))

# /// script
# dependencies = ["numpy"]
# ///
"""Find sizes where the estimate is too small AND the true half-span is an exact tie
whose parity matches a real pixel column (so `<` instead of `<=` would drop a pixel)."""
import numpy as np

f32 = np.float32
hits = []
for h in range(1, 900):
    rows = np.arange(h, dtype=np.int64)
    dy2 = 2 * rows - h + 1
    q = h * h - dy2 * dy2
    sq = np.sqrt(q.astype(f32))
    for w in range(1, 900):
        est = (sq * f32(w) / f32(h)).astype(np.int64)
        limit = w * w * q
        # exact tie: limit divisible by h*h and the quotient a perfect square
        if limit.max() == 0:
            continue
        quo, rem = np.divmod(limit, h * h)
        s = np.floor(np.sqrt(quo.astype(np.float64))).astype(np.int64)
        s = np.where((s + 1) * (s + 1) <= quo, s + 1, s)
        s = np.where(s * s > quo, s - 1, s)
        tie = (rem == 0) & (s * s == quo)
        low = est < s
        parity = (s % 2) == ((w - 1) % 2)
        m = tie & low & parity
        if m.any():
            r = int(np.nonzero(m)[0][0])
            hits.append((w, h, r, int(est[r]), int(s[r])))
            if len(hits) >= 5:
                break
    if len(hits) >= 5:
        break
print(hits)

canvas_fill_ellipse: work each row out in whole numbers (#57)

Every row of every filled circle did a sqrt, a ceil, a floor and a divide in
double, which the S3 does in software; Halftone spent about 80% of its step
there. A pixel is inside when dx2^2*h^2 <= w^2*(h^2 - dy2^2) with distances
doubled to clear the halves, so the row is integers throughout. A float sqrt
only makes the starting guess, and two loops make it exact. Sizes over 32768
(whose squares could overflow 64 bits) keep the old double code.

Shared code, so it is a prototype for Rod to approve: the whole native suite
(796 tests) passes with no pinned frame moved.

Tests: the original double fill is kept as a reference and compared for every
size to 48 at three offsets and for big and clipped sizes; a second check
compares 4,000 random sizes to 3000 against the integer definition itself;
and six sizes found by running the float arithmetic over every size to 400
(the guess is one too big at 220x21, 264x23, 312x25 and one too small at
318x181) pin the correction loops. Mutation-checked: dropping either end's
rounding, a row offset, or either correction loop fails tests. Only < for <=
in the upward loop survives, because no size to 900 has an exact tie where
the guess is low.

Not measured on the device. The step should fall to the cost of the span
writes (about 22 ms for Halftone's 1,150 dots at the PSRAM write rate).

"""diffimg.py old.raw new.raw out.png : old, new and a mask of differing pixels (grown for visibility)"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image, ImageFilter

a, b, out = (Path(p) for p in sys.argv[1:4])


def load(p):
    data = p.read_bytes()
    im = Image.new("RGB", (466, 466))
    px = im.load()
    for i in range(466 * 466):
        v = data[2 * i] | (data[2 * i + 1] << 8)
        r, g, bl = (v >> 11) & 31, (v >> 5) & 63, v & 31
        px[i % 466, i // 466] = (r << 3 | r >> 2, g << 2 | g >> 4, bl << 3 | bl >> 2)
    return im


ia, ib = load(a), load(b)
da, db = a.read_bytes(), b.read_bytes()
mask = Image.new("L", (466, 466), 0)
mp = mask.load()
for i in range(466 * 466):
    if da[2 * i : 2 * i + 2] != db[2 * i : 2 * i + 2]:
        mp[i % 466, i // 466] = 255
grown = mask.filter(ImageFilter.MaxFilter(7))
diff = Image.new("RGB", (466, 466), (0, 0, 0))
diff.paste((255, 40, 40), mask=grown)
sheet = Image.new("RGB", (466 * 3 + 20, 466), (60, 60, 60))

canvas_fill_polygon: exact integer scanline fill, no division per row (#74)

The shim's polygon fill divided in double for every edge on every row, which
the S3 does in software. Vertices are integers, so where an edge crosses a
row's centre line is a rational number, and the first pixel at or right of it
is xlo + ceil(((2k + 1) * dx - dy) / (2 * dy)). Each edge keeps that numerator's
quotient and remainder and adds 2 * dx per row, so there is one division per
edge (to start) and none per row, and no double at all. A pixel on a left edge
is in and one on a right edge is out, whatever the slope. Coordinates beyond
2^24 keep the old double path.

The old fill was not consistent at exact ties (a pixel centre on an edge, as
with any 45 degree edge through integer vertices): float noise in
xi + t * (xj - xi) decided which side won. A new test decides every pixel from
the crossing parity in integers and the old fill failed it on 38 of 120
random polygons; the new one passes, with 10 mutants (nine killed, one
equivalent). The test replaces the comparison with the double reference,
which cannot be the arbiter now, and keeps its sizes up to 1000 vertices.

Shared code, so a prototype for Rod to approve. The whole native suite passes
after two pins moved, both looked at:
- Qix: 612 pixels at frame 200. The old fill left stray black hatch marks
  along a thin sliver polygon; the new frame is clean.
- Pedal: 3 pixels at frame 50, none later.

Not measured on the device.

"""survey_lisa.py program index frames seeds out.txt: counters per frame for seeds."""
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from collections import defaultdict

prog, idx, frames, seeds = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3]), int(sys.argv[4])
tmp = "/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rod-build-stopwatch-screensaver/16383833-c961-4680-b44f-3feb241de877/scratchpad/survey.raw"
by_width = defaultdict(list)
for seed in range(1, seeds + 1):
    env = dict(os.environ, SEED=str(seed), ZZ_COUNT="1")
    r = subprocess.run([prog, idx, str(frames), tmp], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
    m = re.search(r"ZZ width=(\d+) segments=(\d+) spans=(\d+) px=(\d+) points=(\d+)", r.stderr)
    if not m:
        continue
    w, seg, spans, px, pts = map(int, m.groups())
    by_width[w].append((seg / frames, spans / frames, px / frames, pts / frames))
for w in sorted(by_width):
    rows = by_width[w]

### 1. Blank Lines Are Mandatory

Anemone: erase only where last frame's lines were (#59)

Upstream's anemone_draw opens each frame by filling the whole window black,
then draws about 740 short round-capped lines. Counting pixels written on the
host: 229,000 a frame, of which the clear is a full 466 by 466 (217,156) and
the lines about 16,000. A full-frame write to the PSRAM canvas costs about
25 ms on the board, so the clear is most of Anemone's 25-46 ms step: the
stroker's width-6 end caps are not the cost the issue guessed.

The wrapper notes each line's box, grown by its round caps, in a SpanTrack
(hacks/span_erase.h, as Goop does) and the next frame's clear erases only
those spans. Pixels written fall to about 31,000 a frame. The canvas also
marks only those rows dirty, so the push should shrink too (it was always a
full frame).

Frames are byte-identical to before at 1, 2, 50, 200 and 1500 frames (the
pinned hash did not move), and test_push_present's shadow display, which
catches a missed dirty mark, passes. Not measured on the device.

input.content:
stroke: convert a slanted segment's ends straight from int (#98)

slanted() took each endpoint int64 to double and then to float, which is four
__floatdidf and four __truncdfsf2 calls in software on the S3 for every
segment, to feed a float quad. An int under 2^20 is exact as a float, so the
direct conversion gives identical values: frames are unchanged and the whole
native suite passes. The double path stays for ends far off the canvas, where
the clip needs it.

This is the only soft-double left on the stroker's per-segment path. The rest
of stroke.c is already float, and Lisa's step grows with width because it
fills more: on the host Lisa writes 16k pixels and 6.7k spans a frame at
width 2 and 65k pixels and 13k spans at width 8, over 1,396 segments a frame
at every width. Whether the step is fill, spans or per-segment work needs the
device.

input.new_string:
`uv run tools/softdouble_report.py <name>` does that for every object in
  the device build, by function: a count in a per-frame function is a literal
  or a macro the header could not reach. It lists none in Galaxy, Discrete,
  Drift, Flame, Substrate or Interaggregate now.
- Three things hide soft double from `single_precision.h`, each found by that
  report. `frand` (`single_frand.h`) and `MAXRAND`, `M_PI`, `M_PI_2` and
  `M_PI_4` (`single_constants.h`) are macros with a decimal literal in their
  body, past the literal pass; both headers are opt-in, since each moves the
  wrapper's frames and pins. Exponent literals (`1e-6`, `1.0E5`) were skipped
  by `float_literals.py` until Drift and Flame showed one each. And a struct
  declared with `double` fields before the rename keeps them, so a float
  `corners[j].x * size` plus a `double` `pos.x` is a software add: HexTrail's
  `XYZ` (from `normals.h`) was 94 calls in `draw_hextrail`. Give the hack its
  own float struct under the same name, and `normals.h` another name for the
  double one (`hextrail_single_gl.c`; frames byte-identical). To find the line
  of a stray promotion, add `-Wdouble-promotion -fsyntax-only` to a file's
  compile command in `firmware/compile_commands.json` (`pio run -e stopwatch
  -t compiledb`; delete the file afterwards, it upsets the editor).
- `canvas_fill_ellipse` and `canvas_fill_polygon` work in whole numbers, not
  double (the S3 does double in software). The ellipse is exact: a pixel is in
  when `dx2^2 * h^2 <= w^2 * (h^2 - dy2^2)` with distances doubled, and a float
  `sqrt` only starts the search for each row (it is wrong by one at 220 by 21,
  264 by 23, 312 by 25 and 318 by 181, which the tests pin). The polygon steps
  each edge's crossing with a quotient and remainder, no division per row, and
  a pixel on a left edge is in and one on a right edge is out. The old double
  fill was not consistent at exact ties (a 45 degree edge through integer
  vertices): it left stray hatch marks on Qix's thin sliver polygons, so Qix
  and Pedal re-pinned. Sizes or coordinates past 32768 and 2^24 keep the
  double code. Neither is measured on the device yet.

The work is 8 commits on `feature/soft-double-investigation`, in the worktree `.claude/worktrees/soft-double-investigation`. It isn't pushed and has no PR. The full native suite passes (797 of 797), the device build compiles at 49.5% flash, and nothing was flashed.

## Two premises changed

- **#98 (stroker):** `stroke.c` is already float on its hot path, so there is no stroker maths to speed up. I removed the one soft-double spot, a per-segment `int64→double→float` conversion in `slanted` (frames unchanged). Lisa does the same 1,396 segments a frame at every width. Its fill grows from 16k pixels and 6.7k spans at width 2 to 65k and 13k at width 8. Whether that fill or the per-segment work is the cost needs the device.
- **#59 (Anemone):** the end caps weren't the cost. Upstream fills the whole window black every frame, which is about 217k of its 229k pixels written. The wrapper now erases only where the last frame's lines were (the Goop approach). That drops it to 31k pixels a frame, with byte-identical frames at 1, 2, 50, 200 and 1500, and only those rows marked dirty, so the push should shrink too.

## What else landed

- **#57 and #74 (shared canvas code):** `canvas_fill_ellipse` and `canvas_fill_polygon` now use whole numbers, with no double maths per row.
  - **Ellipse:** pixel-identical to the old one, and no pinned frame moved.
  - **Polygon:** the old fill wasn't consistent at exact ties, such as a 45° edge through integer vertices. That left stray hatch marks on a thin sliver in Qix. The new exact fill removes them, so I re-pinned Qix (612 pixels) and Pedal (3 pixels) after looking at the frames.
  - **Tests:** the new ones are mutation-checked. Two mutants survive, both equivalent.
- **#75 and wrapper fixes:**
  - **Interaggregate:** `build_field` was full of `frand` calls. It now has no soft-double calls at all.
  - **Galaxy, Discrete, Drift, Flame, Substrate:** these predated the float-literal pass. They now have none left in per-frame functions, using a new opt-in `single_constants.h` for `MAXRAND` and `M_PI`, plus exponent literals like `1e-6`, which the literal pass had skipped.
  - **HexTrail:** a `double` struct (`XYZ`) was making every hexagon vertex software double (94 calls in its `draw_hextrail`, now 4). Frames are byte-identical.
- **Tooling and notes:** `tools/softdouble_report.py` lists soft-double calls per function from the device objects. `-Wdouble-promotion` points at the exact line. Both are written up in the rules files and the port-hack skill.

## Decisions for you

1. **Shared canvas code:** are you happy to take the ellipse and polygon changes (and the Qix and Pedal re-pins)? They're separate commits, so they can be dropped independently.
2. **Device check:** you'd flash `main` against this branch, one after the other, for Anemone, Lisa at each width, HexTrail, Galaxy, Discrete, Drift, Flame, Substrate and Interaggregate. `ab_flash.py` only varies flags, so it can't compare the two trees. Anemone and the ellipse and polygon fills are where I expect the biggest gains. I have no measured numbers for any of it.
3. **Push and draft PR:** shall I push the branch and open a draft?

## Not done

- **#54:** only idea 5 (Deluxe's `draw_star` in double) is soft-double, and I left it. The other #54 ideas are different problems.
- **Other slow hacks:** several registered hacks still run unwrapped double and are slow in your measured table: Vines 2.8 fps, Forest 1.8, Pedal, Interference 10.2, XSpirograph 11, Kumppa 13.4 and Morph3D. 2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - ESP32-S3 has a single-precision FPU only; `double` ops and libm calls are software (`__muldf3`, `__divdf3`, `sqrt`, ...).
   - `single_precision.h` renames the `double` keyword to `float` and maps libm to the `f` versions. It cannot reach:
     - macros with decimal literals (`frand` in screenhack.h/yarandom.h, `MAXRAND` = `(2147483648.0)`, `M_PI`, `M_PI_2`, `M_PI_4`);

   - Build-time float-literal pass: `firmware/patch_float_literals.py` plus `tools/float_literals.py`, generating `<name>_floatlit.c` in the build dir.

     - A float `sqrt` gives only the starting guess, corrected by two exact loops.
     - Sizes over 32768 keep the old double path.
   - Exact integer polygon fill:
     - Each edge is oriented downward.
     - The first pixel at or right of the crossing is `xlo + ceil(((2k+1)·dx − dy)/(2·dy))`.
     - A quotient and remainder are stepped per row, so there is no division per row.
     - A pixel on a left edge is in and one on a right edge is out.
     - Coordinates beyond 2^24 keep the double path.
   - `span_erase.h` (`SpanTrack`) erases only what the previous frame drew, instead of a full clear (about 25 ms per full-frame PSRAM write).

# Flashing and measuring on the device

Moved verbatim from AGENTS.md.

- `pio run -e stopwatch`: build for the device. Add `-t upload` to flash.
  The device starts on a random hack; to pin one while examining it, prefix
  `PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS='-DSTART_HACK=\"galaxy\"'` (a name from `g_hacks[]`,
  any case; an unknown name falls back to random and logs it). Rebuild without
  it afterwards, since the define sticks to the build. Unescaped quotes fail
  with "error: 'truchet' was not declared in this scope".
  It rotates to the next hack every 90 s (a button press restarts the count);
  `-DROTATE_SECONDS=5` shortens that for leak testing and `=0` turns it off. A
  pinned build still rotates, so add `=0` to measure one hack.
  The log prints `rotate -> <hack> heap= psram=` at each change. Combine flags
  in one `PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS` string.
  `-DBADGE_NAME=\"Rod\ B.\"` sets the name badge text (default "Rod" over
  "Begbie"; `\n` starts a new line). Check a
  flag reached the binary with
  `strings -a -n 3 .pio/build/stopwatch/firmware.elf | grep -c '^Rod B\.$'`:
  plain `strings` skips anything under 4 characters.
  `-DQR_URL=\"https://example.com\"` sets the QR overlay's target (default the
  LinkedIn profile). Check it reached the binary with
  `strings -a .pio/build/stopwatch/firmware.elf | grep -c 'example.com'`.
  In a worktree session the harness refuses backslash-escaped flag values and
  `$(cat file)`. Use `PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS="'-DBADGE_NAME=\"Rod B.\"'
  '-DSTART_HACK=\"gears\"' -DROTATE_SECONDS=0"` with `.venv/bin/pio run -d
  firmware -e stopwatch -t upload` from the worktree root.
- Serial log: read `/dev/cu.usbmodem112401` at 115200 for N seconds into a file
  (a pyserial script run with `.venv/bin/python -I`). Run it in the background
  with absolute paths, since background shells ignore `cd`. Lines to read:
  `run <hack> fps= step= push= sync= wait= rows=` (ms per frame in the hack,
  the push, the wait for the panel's TE edge before a synced push (only
  Unknown Pleasures; not counted in `push=`) and the wait; mean canvas rows
  sent per frame, 466 being a full push,
  though overlay redraws made while waiting can push it higher)
  and `switch -> <hack> press_waited=`. An empty capture, or "Device not
  configured", means the USB port went away and came back (a flash, a crash):
  reopen it in a loop. Opening the port resets the board
  (`rst:0x15 USB_UART_CHIP_RESET`, even with DTR/RTS held low): the overlay
  returns to nothing and a random hack starts. To measure one hack, flash a
  pinned build (`START_HACK` plus `ROTATE_SECONDS=0`), start the capture, then
  tap during it: the early windows are the baseline, the later ones have the
  overlay.
  Set `dtr` and `rts` to False on an unopened `serial.Serial()` before
  `open()`: a reopen loop without that once parked the chip in its bootloader
  (`boot:0x3 ... waiting for download`, screen frozen). Recover, or reset just
  before a capture to log from boot (a hack's `fprintf(stderr)` reaches the
  log), with `.venv/bin/python .platformio/packages/tool-esptoolpy/esptool.py
  --chip esp32s3 --port /dev/cu.usbmodem112401 --after hard_reset read_mac`.

  (Pyro, then Lightning, then Drift...). Work out how long a restart takes
  from the hack's cycle count times its frame time (Substrate: 10,000 cycles
  at about 160 ms is 27 minutes) and capture that long, with rotation off.
- `ad-flyingtoasters` force flags (add to `PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS`):
  `-DAD_TOASTERS_ART=0|1` (0 is 1-bit, 1 is colour) and
  `-DAD_TOASTERS_DONENESS=0|1|2` (light, medium, dark) and
  `-DAD_TOASTERS_SCALE=1|2` (2 is the default, with 6 flyers; 1 is the
  original size, with 10); a number outside those is an `#error`. It logs
  `ad-flyingtoasters: <art>, doneness=<level>` to stderr at start.
- To see where a GL hack's frame goes, add `-DGL_PROFILE`: a `glprof` line
  follows each `run` line with time per stage (clear, list, vertex, shade,
  tri, fill, point, line; nested, so vertex includes tri and fill). Time left
  over is the hack's own code. To compare builds, `.venv/bin/python -I
  tools/ab_flash.py --hack Gears --seconds 60 --rounds 2 --out <dir>
  "a=-DGL_PROFILE" "b=-DGL_PROFILE -DFOO"` builds each variant pinned, flashes
  them in turn and tabulates the windows. It flashes: run it only with Rod's
  go-ahead. It builds each hack's variants from the working tree when that
  hack's turn starts, so leave `src/` and `tools/tinygl_patch.py` alone until

- `esptool` reads of the 16 MB flash need `--baud 921600` (about 3.5 minutes)
  and show no progress when piped.
- Another session may be using the board. Before flashing, run `lsof
  /dev/cu.usbmodem112401`: a "multiple access on port" upload error was
  another session's serial capture, and esptool's connect resets the board
  under it. Ask Rod before flashing over someone else's run.
- PlatformIO cleans the build directory, image and all, when
  `PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS` changes: an `-t nobuild -t upload` with other flags

- `heap=` and `psram=` are the reading at the end of a window, not a minimum:

  with lap 1. PSRAM should match exactly on every visit.
- To prove a device-only path the host cannot run (the ROM's `tinfl`), add a
  temporary `#ifdef` block after `printStats("boot")` in `main.cpp` that logs
  a checksum, compare it with one computed in Python, then `git checkout

"""Flash builds of the firmware in turn and compare their serial logs.

    .venv/bin/python -I tools/ab_flash.py --hack CubicGrid --seconds 60 \\
        --rounds 2 --out /tmp/ab base= iram=-DGL_IRAM "prof=-DGL_PROFILE -DGL_IRAM"

Each `name=flags` is a variant. Every variant is built once, pinned to the
hack with rotation off (`START_HACK`, `ROTATE_SECONDS=0`), and its image kept.
Then, round by round, each image is flashed and the serial log captured for
`--seconds`. A boot is deterministic, so alternating builds and comparing
window by window is how this repo measures a change (AGENTS.md).

This flashes the device: run it only with Rod's go-ahead. It never touches
the partition table or `ffat`; `pio run -t upload` writes what a normal
upload writes.
"""

import argparse
import os
import re
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
FIRMWARE = ROOT / "firmware"

RUN = re.compile(r"^run (?P<hack>\S+) (?P<fields>.*)$")
GLPROF = re.compile(r"^glprof (?P<hack>\S+) (?P<fields>.*)$")
FIELD = re.compile(r"(\w+)=([-\d.]+)")


def parse_fields(text: str) -> dict[str, float]:
    """`fps=12.3 step=45.6ms rows=466` to {"fps": 12.3, "step": 45.6, ...}."""
    return {k: float(v) for k, v in FIELD.findall(text)}


@dataclass
class Capture:
    runs: list[dict[str, float]] = field(default_factory=list)
    glprof: list[dict[str, float]] = field(default_factory=list)


def parse_log(text: str, hack: str) -> Capture:
    """The `run` and `glprof` windows a log has for `hack` (any case)."""
    out = Capture()
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        for pattern, bucket in ((RUN, out.runs), (GLPROF, out.glprof)):
            m = pattern.match(line)
            if m and m.group("hack").lower() == hack.lower():
                bucket.append(parse_fields(m.group("fields")))
    return out


def summarise(windows: list[dict[str, float]], skip: int = 1) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Mean of each field, leaving out the first `skip` windows: the first

"""Makes BinaryRing's random scale a float literal.

`frand1()` is `random() << 1` times 4.65661287524579692411E-10, an exponent
literal, which tools/float_literals.py leaves as a double. Every particle calls

byte-identical; firmware/patch_float_literals.py runs this on its text.
"""

OLD = "4.65661287524579692411E-10)"
NEW = "4.65661287524579692411E-10f)"


def float_random_scale(source: str) -> str:
    found = source.count(OLD)
    if found != 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"expected 1 of `{OLD}` in binaryring.c, found {found}; has upstream changed?"
        )
    return source.replace(OLD, NEW)
/* Builds the unmodified binaryring.c, told the display is 24 bits deep, in

 * time (tools/float_literals.py, and tools/binaryring_patch.py for the
 * exponent literal in frand1).
 *
 * The hack blends each anti-aliased hit into its own buffer of pixel values
 * at an alpha of 0.15 times the coverage. In its 16-bit path a hit adds less
 * than one 5-bit step of red or blue, which is dropped, so only green ever
 * builds up and the picture stays a dim green. In its 24-bit path (0xRRGGBB,
 * as on most X displays) the hits accumulate, so the wrapper gives it that
 * depth.
 *
 * Each pixel it writes to its XImage goes straight to the window instead,
 * packed to the canvas's byte-swapped RGB565, and the frame's XPutImage into a
 * pixmap and XCopyArea to the window are skipped: the window then holds what
 * the copy would have put there. Those two full-frame copies took 130 of a
 * 240 ms step on the board (the XImage is 32 bits a pixel, which XPutImage
 * copies a pixel at a time), and they marked every row for the push. */

#include <stdint.h>

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

import xspirograph_patch as xp
import xs_vendor

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
UPSTREAM = xs_vendor.upstream(ROOT) / "hacks" / "xspirograph.c"

SAMPLE = """\
static Bool
go (struct state *st, int radius1, int radius2, int d)
{
  return cos(1.0);
}

#define min(a,b) ((a)<(b)?(a):(b))
"""


def test_go_is_replaced_and_the_rest_kept():
    out = xp.reduce_the_angles(SAMPLE)
    assert "% 360" in out
    assert "return cos(1.0);" not in out
    assert "#define min(a,b)" in out


def test_both_angles_are_reduced_before_the_multiply():
    out = xp.reduce_the_angles(SAMPLE)
    assert "spin = st->theta % 360;" in out
    assert "roll = (((radius1 * st->theta) - delta) / radius2) % 360;" in out


def test_it_refuses_a_source_without_go():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="upstream"):
        xp.reduce_the_angles("int x;\n")


def test_it_refuses_go_twice():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="upstream"):
        xp.reduce_the_angles(SAMPLE + SAMPLE)


@pytest.mark.skipif(not UPSTREAM.exists(), reason=f"needs {xs_vendor.UPSTREAM}")
def test_upstream_has_go_once_and_keeps_its_neighbours():
    text = UPSTREAM.read_text()
    out = xp.reduce_the_angles(text)
    assert out.count("roll = ") == 1
    assert "static void\npick_new" in out
    assert "#define min(a,b)" in out

"""Lists the software-double calls in the device build's objects, by function.

The ESP32-S3's FPU is single-precision only, so `double` arithmetic and libm
calls become library calls (`__muldf3`, `sqrt`, ...) that cost tens to hundreds
of cycles. A wrapper that still shows them in a per-frame function has a
literal or a macro the single-precision header could not reach (`frand`,
`MAXRAND`, `M_PI`). This reads what the compiler produced, so it needs a device
build: `pio run -e stopwatch` from `firmware/`.

    uv run tools/softdouble_report.py              # every hack object
    uv run tools/softdouble_report.py galaxy_single x11shim/stroke
"""

import re
import subprocess
import sys
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OBJDUMP = next(
    (ROOT / ".platformio/packages/toolchain-xtensa-esp32s3/bin").glob(
        "xtensa-esp32s3-elf-objdump"
    ),
    None,
)
BUILD = ROOT / "firmware/.pio/build/stopwatch/src"

SOFT = re.compile(
    r"R_XTENSA_\w+\s+(__\w*df\w*|sqrt|floor|ceil|sin|cos|pow|atan2?|log|exp)\s*$"
)
FUNCTION = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]+ <(.+)>:")


def soft_calls(obj: Path) -> dict[str, Counter]:
    """Soft-double references per function in one object file."""
    assert OBJDUMP is not None, "toolchain not found: link .platformio into the repo"
    listing = subprocess.run(
        [str(OBJDUMP), "-dr", "--no-show-raw-insn", str(obj)],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    ).stdout
    found: dict[str, Counter] = defaultdict(Counter)
    function = None
    for line in listing.splitlines():
        if m := FUNCTION.match(line):
            function = m.group(1)
        elif (
            function
            and not function.startswith(".literal")
            and (m := SOFT.search(line))
        ):
            found[function][m.group(1)] += 1
    return found


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    if not BUILD.is_dir():
        raise SystemExit(f"no device build at {BUILD}: run pio run -e stopwatch")

        s.port = "/dev/cu.usbmodem112401"
        s.baudrate = 115200
        s.timeout = 1
        s.dtr = False

        try:
            s.open()
            while time.time() < end:
                line = s.readline()
                if line:
                    f.write(line.decode("utf-8", "replace"))

            time.sleep(1)
        finally:

input.content:
"""Ranks the hacks in a serial log of one rotation lap by where their time goes.

Flash a build with `-DROTATE_SECONDS=20`, log the serial port for the whole lap
(about 20 seconds a hack), then:

    uv run tools/triage_hacks.py lap.log
    uv run tools/triage_hacks.py lap.log --soft    # add soft-double call counts

A frame is `step` (the hack), `push` (the display) and `wait` (what is left of
the delay the hack asked for after the push is credited). Each hack is put in
the first class that fits:

- paced: `wait` is longer than `step`, so the hack asked for its rate. A faster
  step changes nothing unless the delay is also changed (Forest, Vines).
- push-bound: `push` is longer than `step`. Only fewer rows or a smaller push
  help.
- step-bound: `step` is the biggest part. These are the ones to look into.

`--soft` reads the device build's objects (`pio run -e stopwatch` first) for
the soft-double calls in the hack's own object, so a step-bound hack with a
count is a wrapper candidate. A hack the table calls step-bound with no calls
is in its drawing, not its maths.
"""

import argparse
import re
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

RUN = re.compile(r"^run (?P<hack>\S+) (?P<fields>.*)$")
FIELD = re.compile(r"(\w+)=([-\d.]+)")


@dataclass
class Row:
    hack: str
    windows: int
    fps: float
    worst_fps: float
    step: float
    push: float
    wait: float
    kind: str


def parse(text: str) -> dict[str, list[dict[str, float]]]:
    """The `run` windows for each hack, in order."""
    out: dict[str, list[dict[str, float]]] = defaultdict(list)
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        if m := RUN.match(raw.strip()):
            fields = {k: float(v) for k, v in FIELD.findall(m.group("fields"))}
            out[m.group("hack")].append(fields)
    return out


def classify(step: float, push: float, wait: float) -> str:
    if wait > step:
        return "paced"
    if push > step:
        return "push-bound"
    return "step-bound"


def summarise(runs: dict[str, list[dict[str, float]]], skip: int = 1) -> list[Row]:
    """One row a hack. The first window holds the boot and the name overlay, so
    it is left out when the hack has more than one."""
    rows = []
    for hack, windows in runs.items():
        kept = windows[skip:] or windows

        def mean(key: str) -> float:
            return sum(w.get(key, 0.0) for w in kept) / len(kept)

        step, push, wait = mean("step"), mean("push"), mean("wait")
        rows.append(
            Row(
                hack,
                len(kept),
                mean("fps"),
                min(w.get("fps", 0.0) for w in kept),
                step,
                push,
                wait,
                classify(step, push, wait),
            )
        )
    return rows


def soft_counts() -> dict[str, int]:
    """Soft-double calls per object stem, from the device build."""
    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
    import softdouble_report as sd

    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    for obj in sd.BUILD.rglob("*.o"):
        if "hacks/" not in str(obj):
            continue
        found = sd.soft_calls(obj)
        counts[obj.name.split(".")[0]] = sum(sum(c.values()) for c in found.values())
    return counts


def soft_for(hack: str, counts: dict[str, int]) -> int:
    """The calls in objects whose name starts with the hack's, in any wrapper."""
    key = hack.lower()
    return sum(n for stem, n in counts.items() if stem.startswith(key))


def render(rows: list[Row], counts: dict[str, int] | None) -> str:
    order = {"step-bound": 0, "push-bound": 1, "paced": 2}
    rows = sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (order[r.kind], -r.step))
    head = "| Hack | Class | fps | worst | step | push | wait |"
    rule = "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |"
    if counts is not None:
        head += " soft |"
        rule += " --- |"
    lines = [head, rule]
    for r in rows:
        line = (
            f"| {r.hack} | {r.kind} | {r.fps:.1f} | {r.worst_fps:.1f} | "
            f"{r.step:.1f} ms | {r.push:.1f} ms | {r.wait:.1f} ms |"
        )
        if counts is not None:
            line += f" {soft_for(r.hack, counts)} |"
        lines.append(line)
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("log", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--soft", action="store_true", help="add soft-double counts")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    rows = summarise(parse(args.log.read_text(errors="replace")))
    sys.stdout.write(render(rows, soft_counts() if args.soft else None))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

import triage_hacks as th

LOG = """\
boot noise
run Vines fps=2.0 step=180.0ms push=3.0ms sync=0.0ms wait=190.0ms rows=80
run Vines fps=2.6 step=182.0ms push=1.0ms sync=0.0ms wait=180.0ms rows=80
run Vines fps=2.8 step=184.0ms push=1.0ms sync=0.0ms wait=178.0ms rows=80
run Gears fps=5.0 step=30.0ms push=40.0ms sync=0.0ms wait=0.0ms rows=466
run Gears fps=6.0 step=40.0ms push=30.0ms sync=0.0ms wait=0.0ms rows=466
run Gears fps=8.0 step=60.0ms push=30.0ms sync=0.0ms wait=0.0ms rows=466
run Pyro fps=30.0 step=1.0ms push=31.0ms sync=0.0ms wait=0.0ms rows=466
"""


def test_it_collects_windows_per_hack_and_ignores_other_lines():
    runs = th.parse(LOG)
    assert sorted(runs) == ["Gears", "Pyro", "Vines"]
    assert [w["fps"] for w in runs["Vines"]] == [2.0, 2.6, 2.8]


def test_a_longer_wait_than_step_is_paced():
    assert th.classify(step=10, push=3, wait=11) == "paced"


def test_a_longer_push_than_step_is_push_bound():
    assert th.classify(step=10, push=31, wait=0) == "push-bound"


def test_otherwise_the_step_is_the_bottleneck():
    assert th.classify(step=50, push=31, wait=0) == "step-bound"


def test_equal_step_and_wait_is_not_paced():
    assert th.classify(step=10, push=3, wait=10) == "step-bound"


def test_the_first_window_is_left_out():
    rows = {r.hack: r for r in th.summarise(th.parse(LOG))}
    assert rows["Vines"].fps == 2.7
    assert rows["Vines"].worst_fps == 2.6
    assert rows["Gears"].step == 50.0


def test_a_hack_with_one_window_keeps_it():
    rows = {r.hack: r for r in th.summarise(th.parse(LOG))}
    assert rows["Pyro"].fps == 30.0


def test_step_bound_hacks_come_first_slowest_step_first():
    out = th.render(th.summarise(th.parse(LOG)), None).splitlines()
    names = [line.split("|")[1].strip() for line in out[2:]]
    assert names == ["Gears", "Pyro", "Vines"]


def test_soft_counts_add_every_object_that_starts_with_the_hack_name():
    counts = {"xspirograph_single": 4, "xspirograph": 40, "vines_single": 2}
    assert th.soft_for("XSpirograph", counts) == 44
    assert th.soft_for("Vines", counts) == 2

input.new_string:
calling `canvas_fill_ellipse` (which used to do `double` maths per row, in
  software on the S3; see below). A test pins the pixels to
  `canvas_fill_ellipse`.
- `canvas_fill_ellipse` and `canvas_fill_polygon` work in whole numbers, not
  double (the S3 does double in software). The ellipse is exact: a pixel is in
  when `dx2^2 * h^2 <= w^2 * (h^2 - dy2^2)` with distances doubled, and a float
  `sqrt` only starts the search for each row (it is wrong by one at 220 by 21,
  264 by 23, 312 by 25 and 318 by 181, which the tests pin). The polygon steps
  each edge's crossing with a quotient and remainder, no division per row, and
  a pixel on a left edge is in and one on a right edge is out. The old double
  fill was not consistent at exact ties (a 45 degree edge through integer
  vertices): it left stray hatch marks on Qix's thin sliver polygons, so Qix
  (612 pixels) and Pedal (3) re-pinned. Sizes or coordinates past 32768 and
  2^24 keep the double code. On the board (step, before to after): Bouboule
  14.5 to 5.2 ms (27.4 to 36.8 fps), Qix 14.6 to 1.9 ms (37.3 to 70.1 fps),
  Pedal 21.8 to 8.6 ms (it then holds the picture for 5 s).
- Lisa is the counter-example to "the stroker maths is the cost" (#98).
  `stroke.c`'s hot path was already float, and converting a slanted segment's
  ends from int straight to float moved Lisa by nothing (52.1 ms before and
  after). With the line calls compiled out its step is 5.2 ms, so 47 ms of 52
  is drawing: 1,396 segments, 6.7k spans and 16k pixels a frame at width 2 and
  13k spans and 65k pixels at width 8. About 3.6 us a span against about 0.1
  us a pixel in a sequential full-frame write suggests each scattered span pays
  a PSRAM cache-line miss (a cost per line touched, not per pixel). Not
  proved: the way to test it is the PSRAM and data-cache settings (speed, line
  size, cache size), which no hack can change.

input.new_string:
wrapper's object for `__muldf3` and friends with `xtensa-esp32s3-elf-nm`.
  `uv run tools/softdouble_report.py <name>` does that for every object in
  the device build, by function: a count in a per-frame function is a literal
  or a macro the header could not reach. It lists none in Galaxy, Discrete,
  Drift, Flame, Substrate or Interaggregate now.
- Four things hide soft double from `single_precision.h`, each found by that
  report. `frand` (`single_frand.h`) and `MAXRAND`, `M_PI`, `M_PI_2` and
  `M_PI_4` (`single_constants.h`) are macros with a decimal literal in their
  body, past the literal pass; both headers are opt-in, since each moves the
  wrapper's frames and pins. Exponent literals (`1e-6`, `1.0E5`) were skipped
  by `float_literals.py` until Drift and Flame showed one each. A struct
  declared with `double` fields before the rename keeps them, so a float
  `corners[j].x * size` plus a `double` `pos.x` is a software add: HexTrail's
  `XYZ` (from `normals.h`) was 94 calls in `draw_hextrail`. Give the hack its
  own float struct under the same name, and `normals.h` another name for the
  double one (`hextrail_single_gl.c`; frames byte-identical). And a trig
  argument that is a big whole number cannot be a float: XSpirograph's second
  angle is millions of degrees and Vines' is an `int` in the billions, so a
  plain `double` to `float` turned both pictures to noise. XSpirograph reduces
  its angles mod 360 in integers at build time (`tools/xspirograph_patch.py`);
  Vines builds `(double) a` as `(long) a`, so its `cos` macro gets the exact
  integer and takes the phase as a 64-bit multiply by 2^64 / 2 pi, wrapping
  into whole turns (`vines_single.c`). Look at a frame before trusting a
  float build of anything whose angles grow. To find the line of a stray
  promotion, add `-Wdouble-promotion -fsyntax-only` to a file's compile
